record.model: learned (LightGBM) minutes x usage x teammates out x opponent-by-position x market team total, trained only on earlier seasons

findings.title: Locksmith's picks: the early spread
findings.text: Betting the OPENING spread when Locksmith disagreed by 3+ points went 2373-1853 for +304 units (+7.2%), profitable in 6 of 6 seasons, and beat the closing line 69% of the time. Rules were chosen each season from earlier seasons only, and the model used only the lineup known when the line opened.

findings.title: Close to the closing line, not better
findings.text: Locksmith misses the final margin by 10.91 points on average; the closing spread misses by 10.67. The closing line knows late injury news and sharp money, so Locksmith's edge is betting before the line gets there.

findings.title: Early totals don't work
findings.text: Unlike hockey, betting NBA totals at the opener when Locksmith disagreed lost money (about +10.0%). Locksmith only bets NBA spreads.

findings.title: At the game-day line, the edge is gone
findings.text: The early-spread record assumes every bet was placed at the opening spread. The same kind of bets (3+ points off the opener) graded at the line available on game day won 50.0% of 2,050 (-4.6% at -110), against 54.0% at the opener. Locksmith sees where the line is going, but once it gets there nothing is left. So a basketball pick is shown only while today's line is still the opening number (or better).

findings.title: Honest chances: what bets like this actually won
findings.text: The simulator alone is over-confident (it gives many spreads 60-66% to cover). So every pick shows the chance that early spread bets with the same disagreement actually covered: 1.5-3 points 52%, 3-4.5 points 54%, 4.5-6 points 53%, 6-8 points 55%, 8+ points 54% (4,213 bets). October and November bets have done better (54%, 61% at 4.5+ points): the market is slowest to adjust early in the season.

findings.title: Player projections rebuilt: who is out, the matchup, the game
findings.text: A learned model now projects every player's minutes and stats from who is out tonight (and how many minutes and shots leave with them), the opponent's defence against his position, the market's team total and spread (blowouts cost starters minutes), rest and recent form. Tested season by season on 111,235 player-games (each season by a model trained only on earlier ones): average miss 4.41 points (old model 4.67, recent average 4.71), 1.84 rebounds, 1.29 assists, and 4.4 minutes (recent average 5.3).

findings.title: Player props: tested on every real line, no plays until the record says so
findings.text: Every DraftKings over/under this season (18,699 lines, 181 games so far) is graded at its opening line and price; DraftKings' latest prices on finished games can be in-game prices, so they are not used. So far Locksmith is about as accurate as DraftKings' opener on its own (0.687 vs 0.686, lower is better) and better combined with it, and pre-game price moves went Locksmith's way 60% of the time. A prop becomes a play only when a rule has made money on earlier days (150+ bets over 25+ games and 7+ days); 58 rule(s) qualify now.

findings.title: Who plays matters
findings.text: Every stint since 2018 (about 300,000 of them, rebuilt from substitutions) measures each player's impact per 100 possessions, adjusted for teammates and opponents and anchored to his box score. Tonight's lineup vs a team's normal lineup is in the model. Highest impact right now: Victor Wembanyama, Nikola Jokic, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Kawhi Leonard, Chet Holmgren.

findings.title: Live odds
findings.text: The live win probability (trained on every play of 2018-19 to 2024-25) scores 0.443 on 2025-26 (pregame line alone: 0.582). For the live total, simply scaling the pregame total by time left was more accurate than a learned model, so that is what Locksmith uses.
